learningObjective: Determine the degree of shared-memory bank conflict for a stride access pattern and its throughput impact.
stem: A CUDA kernel declares `__shared__ float smem[32][32]` (32 banks × 4-byte bank width on Ampere). After a `__syncthreads()`, the block reads `smem[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y]` with a 32×32 thread block. What is the resulting bank-conflict behavior for a warp with a single value of threadIdx.y (threads share y, differ in x)?

options.text: No conflict: threads in a warp read column `y` from rows `0..31`; each row starts on a different bank, so all 32 threads target distinct banks in one cycle.
The compiler automatically pads the shared-memory declaration to avoid conflicts, so this access pattern is transparently conflict-free.
16-way conflict: half-warp granularity limits shared-memory conflicts to at most 16-way on Ampere.

32-way conflict: threads in the warp read a single column `y`, i.e., addresses smem[0][y], smem[1][y], ..., smem[31][y]. Each of these lies in the same bank because 32 × 4 B row stride is a multiple of the bank stride (32×4 B), serializing to 32 accesses.

explanation: Option D is correct; options A, B, C are incorrect. A (Wrong): with a 32-wide row of 4-byte elements, the row stride matches the bank period (128 B = 32 banks × 4 B), so column-major access hits the same bank across rows. B (Wrong): shared-memory padding must be programmer-written (e.g., declare [32][33]). C (Wrong): half-warp granularity applied to legacy architectures (Fermi and earlier); Ampere uses warp-wide conflict analysis. D (Correct): the access serializes to 32 cycles due to same-bank targeting. General context: Ampere shared memory has 32 banks with 4-byte width; bank = (address / 4) mod 32. For smem[i][y] with row size 32 floats (128 B), the byte address is i·128 + y·4. The bank index (i·128 + y·4)/4 mod 32 = (i·32 + y) mod 32 = y (since i·32 mod 32 = 0). All 32 threads in the warp map to the same bank y → 32-way conflict; access serializes into 32 cycles. Padding to [32][33] (or transposing the access) restores conflict-free behavior.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: with a 32-wide row of 4-byte elements, the row stride matches the bank period (128 B = 32 banks × 4 B), so column-major access hits the same bank across rows.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: shared-memory padding must be programmer-written (e.g., declare [32][33]).
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: half-warp granularity applied to legacy architectures (Fermi and earlier); Ampere uses warp-wide conflict analysis.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: the access serializes to 32 cycles due to same-bank targeting.

assumptions: 32 banks × 4 B bank width (default on modern NVIDIA compute capabilities).
Warp is 32 threads with threadIdx.x varying and threadIdx.y constant.
No compiler transformation altering the declared layout.
nonImplications: Does not imply the kernel is unusable at 32-way conflict; the impact is on throughput, not correctness.
Does not imply that padding to [32][33] is universally the right fix; some kernels prefer swizzled addressing or transposed staging.
